name: Continuity Engine
description: The single narration-timed production engine. It can render independent illustrated scenes, explainer boards, or a character-continuity chain; the project chooses the reference behavior while the Series Formula controls narration, perspective, and subject.

idea.systemPromptRole: You are helping generate episode ideas that can be expressed as a sequence of concrete, visualizable narration-timed scenes. The Series Formula sets the subject domain, voice, perspective, title shape, and hook policy.
idea.guidanceText: Each idea should imply a clear sequence of places, actions, objects, or visual beats. Be concrete enough for a scene planner without forcing a character, a first-person voice, or a fixed hook pattern.

script.systemPromptRole: You are writing natural spoken narration with clear, concrete visual beats for a scene planner. The Series Formula sets the perspective, narrator voice, structure, and opening policy. Use people, locations, objects, decisions, and changes that can be rendered scene-by-scene without forcing a recurring character where none is needed.
additionalRules: Keep the Series Formula's perspective and narrator voice consistent throughout.
Anchor the narration to concrete, visualizable actions, locations, objects, or changes — the planner turns these into scenes.
Prefer short, punchy sentences over long abstract ones; busy passages should imply faster cuts.
When the project uses character continuity, keep the recurring on-screen persona consistent; otherwise allow the Formula's subject matter to determine the visual cast.
pacingArc: Opening: establish the specific subject in the Formula's approved voice
Context: make the situation legible with an establishing visual beat
Body: develop the explanation, story, or experience through distinct concrete beats
Turn: show the constraint, comparison, consequence, or new understanding
Close: give the Formula's appropriate resolution without an artificial cliffhanger
script.closingHint: End with a specific resolution, implication, or invitation appropriate to the Series Formula.

narratorStyles.label: Clear conversational narrator
narratorStyles.description: Natural, direct narration; the Series Formula may replace this with its own voice choices.

narratorStyles.label: High-energy
narratorStyles.description: Faster, punchier, motivational — leans into momentum and quick wins.

narratorStyles.label: Calm and deliberate
narratorStyles.description: Measured, confident, 'let me walk you through this' pacing. Good for thoughtful walkthroughs.

imagePrompts.purposeNote: (populated by the Scene Plan page — the LLM produces one visual prompt per planned scene, paced to the user-set min/max scene length. Character references are used only when the project selects character continuity.)
imagePrompts.visualStyleHint: Describe the subject, location, action, and visual hierarchy for this beat. Preserve a recurring character, wardrobe, and setting only when the project uses character continuity.
imagePrompts.defaultStyleTag: Cohesive, grounded, slightly cinematic scene design. Maintain visual continuity across the episode; preserve the same person only when a character reference is active.

thumbnail.conceptGuidance: A cover with one unmistakable episode subject, a strong visual hierarchy, and a composition that matches the selected thumbnail recipe. Use a recurring character only when the project calls for one.
compositionRules: The episode's central subject is large and immediately readable
Visual style is consistent with the rest of the episode
Use the selected thumbnail recipe's title placement and hierarchy
avoid: a recurring character when the episode has no character-continuity requirement

metadata.purposeNote: for a Series Formula rendered with the Continuity Engine
metadata.titleStyleHint: Clear and specific to the subject — say what the episode is actually about. No hype words, no all-caps, no manufactured urgency.
metadata.tagsContext: for the project's selected Series Formula
tagsHookRules: No "#" prefix — these are YouTube tags, not hashtags.

youtubeDescriptionStructure.supportSection: Subscribe for more episodes from this channel.
youtubeDescriptionStructure.aiDisclosure:
🤖 AI DISCLOSURE:
Visuals assembled with AI tools; scenes are rendered to match the narration.
